groups.title: Node IDs drop the file extension (and doc IDs the path), so distinct entities in x.py/x.html or a/x.md/b/x.md collide and one is lost

landed.note: Applied to v8 by the maintainer, authorship kept.

4371.summary: Reword the id-collision warning so it says what the merge did, instead of claiming a document was lost.
4371.why: The warning claimed that "the dropped node is lost" and that the id "does not identify a single entity", for every such collision. On the reporter's corpus that was wrong: none of their 16 remaining warnings was a lost document. They were one entity described in two documents, or a reference to another file, and merging them was correct.
4371.what: The cross-file branch of the warning now says which node was kept and which was merged into it. The wording then depends on where the id came from: a file path (a reference to the kept file, or a separate document), or neither (probably one entity described in both files). It does not change which node survives.
4371.helps: Whoever reads the collision warning gets text that matches what the merge actually did. The severity stays WARNING.
4371.before: [graphify] WARNING: node 'sender' is minted by two different files — keeping 'Sender' from 'docs/a.md', dropping 'sender service' from 'docs/b.md'. An ID is derived from the source path plus the entity name, so this one does not identify a single entity and the dropped node is lost.
4371.after: [graphify] WARNING: node 'sender' is minted by two different files: kept 'Sender' from 'docs/a.md', merged 'sender service' from 'docs/b.md' into it. The id comes from neither path, so this is probably one entity described in both files. The merged node's own label and attributes are not kept; its edges stay on the kept node.
limits: The text cannot tell a reference from a second document when the id comes from a path. It says both are possible. Telling them apart needs edge evidence and is out of scope here (it is the separate fix for the path-qualified id case in #4281).
"Probably one entity" for an id that comes from neither path is an inference, not a fact. Two real documents can also share such an id; the merged node's label and attributes are then lost.
Severity stays WARNING. The reporter asked for something milder, but test_issue_3472 asserts WARNING for a non-path id, so lowering it would change an existing test.

4362.summary: Give each file its own path-qualified id when a dropped folder makes two real documents share a bare id, but keep a reference to another document as one node.
4362.why: Semantic extraction sometimes drops the folder from an id, so a/x.md and b/x.md both emit x. Dedup then merged them and one real document was lost.
4362.what: When files with different paths share a bare id, each file's node is renamed to its path-qualified id (a_x, b_x), unless the bare id is only a mention of another document. A mention is a node that another node of its own file points at with a references edge, and whose id is a shorter path slice of its file. Mentions also lose survivor ties in the collision ranking, so a real document outranks them.
4362.helps: Two real documents with the same bare id stay two nodes instead of one being dropped. A reference to another document no longer becomes a second document or a self-link.
4362.before: a/x.md emits x and b/x.md emits x: dedup keeps one node and b/x.md is dropped (one real document lost).
4362.after: a/x.md emits x and b/x.md emits x: two nodes, a_x and b_x, with edges following their own file.
limits: The mention evidence is inferred from the edges an LLM chose to emit. A missing or reversed references edge gives no evidence, so both files are renamed (R_noedge). With a reversed edge, the reference can still end up as a self-link.
A real document whose own node is linked to its file-level id the same way (an entity named like its file) reads as a mention, and that collision collapses as on v8.
R_toplevel stays wrong: with a top-level protocol.md that also mints protocol, one real document is still dropped by the label tiebreak. It is a separate collision, and a test pins today's result.

If two or more other files also mint the mention's id, the mention stays on the bare id and build_from_json folds it into its own file's page, which gives a self-link and no warning. This is the same outcome as the first version of this PR.
A reference to the bare id from a third file (c.md -> x) cannot be attributed to one file. The edge is left on x, one warning is printed per id, and build() then drops it because no node x exists.

For imports, imports_from and re_exports edges, build_from_json mints an external stub node for the missing target. An import-family edge to a renamed bare id leaves a phantom external node x. Checked by hand; there is no test.

Absolute source_file values (no root, outside the root, or a Windows path on POSIX) are never qualified, so checkout paths cannot leak into ids (#502, #2197, #2618). Those collisions stay on collapse-and-warn.
AST-tier nodes are not touched. Hyperedge members given as dicts are not rewritten, as in the #4282 pass.

cases.correct: 2 nodes; the firmware doc references docs/protocol.md
cases.before: ok, because the mention's label is shorter

cases.correct: no x; c.md's edge not pinned on one file
cases.before: c_note pinned on a_x as EXTRACTED, b/x.md dropped
